title: Thirteen Years and One Flawed Stone
subtitle: 珠宝与矿物 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 珠宝与矿物（科学与技术·矿物与宝石）
meta: 主题语境：珠宝与矿物（科学与技术·矿物与宝石）　|　核心词汇：diamond　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 diamond 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 the cutter ① cut a diamond that no dealer in the city would have bought, and he said the cutting was the whole of the trade. The ② diamond, meaning the stone and not the shape, ran thirteen years and stayed unpolished in the tray; a diamond, he said, is the only thing in a workshop that is judged by how long it is left uncut.

Every ③ diamond in that tray had the same flaw at the heart of it, and the ④ diamond at the end, meaning the one they kept for the ring and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever weighed twice. A diamond, his apprentice said, is nine parts light and one part somebody willing to cut; the cutter said the light is the part that fills thirteen years.

The surveyor meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the diamond was the whole of the field, meaning the shape and not the stone. The ⑥ diamond, meaning the shape and not any of that, is the only thing in a field that everybody marks out and nobody questions; diamond, she said, is either something you cut or the only word that means both a stone and a shape. She said the shape is the part they remember.

By 1957 the ⑦ diamond had become a line in a valuation, and the valuation had become an argument about the flaw. The ⑧ diamond of the whole thing, the cutter wrote in April, was one tray and thirteen years of cutting; diamond, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to cut. She said the cutting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ diamond I remember is the one at the end, which was sold in 1969 and is still described as the strangest in the city. A ⑩ diamond, the apprentice said in 1971, is the only thing that improves by being cut; every diamond, she said, is a shape that has agreed to look like a stone. She said the shape was the honest half.

task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 钻石；金刚石（指盘里放着的那颗）
B. n. 钻石（指那颗宝石本身，与那个菱形相对）
C. 固定搭配：cut a diamond 切割一颗钻石

F. n. 钻石（指估价单上写到、被列名的那颗）
G. n. 菱形（指场地里划出的那个形状）
H. n. 菱形（抽象总称，指人人划出却无人追问的那个）

diamond 意为“钻石”，指那颗宝石本身而不是那个菱形，它在盘里放了十三年而没有抛光。
diamond 意为“钻石”，指那个盘里每一颗钻石，每一颗中心都有同一处瑕疵。
diamond 意为“钻石”，指留给戒指用的那颗，是唯一有人称过两次的。
diamond 意为“菱形”，指场地里划出的那个形状，测量员说这个菱形就是那块场地的全部。
diamond 意为“菱形”，指人人划出却无人追问的那个而不是那颗宝石，是场地里人人都划出、却无人追问的东西。
diamond 意为“钻石”，指估价单上写到、被列名的那颗，到 1957 年这颗钻石成了估价单里的一行。
diamond 意为“钻石、金刚石”，切割师四月写道，整件事的琢磨是一盘宝石和十三年的切割。
diamond 意为“钻石”，我记得的是末尾那一颗，1969 年售出，至今仍被说成全城最奇的一颗。
diamond 为抽象总称，学徒 1971 年说，一颗钻石是唯一会因为被切割而变得更好的东西。
